warning.title: Before you continue
warning.intro: Wavekeep is an unofficial tool and is not affiliated with Deezer or Spotify. Please read this first.

legal.title: Personal use only
legal.text: Downloading from Deezer or Spotify may violate their terms of service and copyright law in your country. Only download music you are allowed to keep, and do not share the files.

account.title: Your accounts are at risk
account.text: Services can restrict or suspend accounts they detect using download tools. Consider using a secondary account instead of your main one.

credentials.title: Protect your login
credentials.text: Your Deezer ARL works like a password, so never share it. Spotify uses a browser login, and Wavekeep never sees your Spotify password.

unofficial.title: Unofficial and unsupported
unofficial.text: Wavekeep relies on interfaces that Deezer and Spotify can change or block at any time, so features may stop working without notice.

accounts.title: Which account do I need?
accounts.text: Deezer needs the ARL cookie of your Deezer account. Spotify needs its own Spotify account and a browser login. Deezer Free accounts are limited to MP3 128 kbps; Premium unlocks MP3 320 and FLAC. What Spotify delivers depends on your account and on the track.

files.title: Where are my files?
files.text: Downloads go to the folder chosen in Settings, by default a Wavekeep folder inside your Music folder. Tags and cover art are embedded, and you can edit them later with the Tag Editor. If you used Deezy, your existing download folder is kept.

log.title: Something went wrong?
log.text: Wavekeep keeps a diagnostic log named wavekeep-debug.log in Wavekeep's logs folder. It stays on your computer and is never uploaded. Passwords, your ARL and login tokens are never written to it, and your home folder appears as ~. It does include track IDs, artist and title, and the paths of your downloads. Use the buttons below to copy it or open its folder when you report a problem.

report.q: How do I report a problem?
report.a: Open Info & FAQ, press Copy recent log, and paste it with a short description into a GitHub issue or the Discord server. The log stays on your computer until you share it yourself, and it never contains your password, ARL or login tokens.

deezy.q: I used Deezy. Will I lose anything?
deezy.a: No. Wavekeep is the new name of Deezy. The first time it starts, it moves your settings, download history, themes, and saved Deezer and Spotify logins over from Deezy. If you installed it with the .exe installer, start Wavekeep once before you uninstall Deezy.

legal.q: Is it legal to use Wavekeep?
legal.a: That depends on your country and on what you do with the files. Wavekeep cannot check this for you. Treat downloads as personal copies, and respect the services' terms and local copyright law.

ban.a: It is possible, because automated downloading can trigger restrictions. Use a secondary account if the account matters to you, and keep downloads modest and spaced out with Pause Between Downloads and Download Speed Limit in Settings.

arl.q: How do I get my Deezer ARL?
arl.a: Log in to deezer.com in your browser, open the developer tools, and copy the value of the cookie named arl. Paste it in Settings. Treat it like a password.

quality.q: Why can't I download FLAC or 320 kbps?
quality.a: On Deezer, FLAC and 320 kbps need a Premium account. On Spotify, lossless FLAC needs Premium and each track only offers the formats Spotify serves. The Downloads view shows the quality you actually got.

rateLimit.q: Spotify search says the rate limit was reached (429)
rateLimit.a: Wavekeep's default Spotify Client ID is shared by every librespot user, so its search quota can run out. Create an app in the Spotify Developer Dashboard (developer.spotify.com) with the redirect URI http://127.0.0.1:5588/login, paste its Client ID under Settings → Spotify, then disconnect and connect again.

twoLogins.q: Why does Spotify ask me to log in twice?
twoLogins.a: With your own Client ID, search uses your app and downloads use the shared default Client ID, so two browser logins are needed. Approve both.

failed.q: A download failed. What can I do?
failed.a: Press Retry in Downloads. For Deezer, check that your ARL is still valid in Settings. For Spotify, disconnect and connect again. If it keeps failing, press Copy recent log on the Important tab and include it in your report.

tags.q: How do I edit tags or cover art?
tags.a: Use the Tag Editor in the sidebar, or the pencil button next to a finished download. MP3, FLAC, OGG and M4A files are supported.

privacy.a: No. It has no analytics or telemetry and only talks to Deezer and Spotify. Your ARL and Spotify tokens are kept in your operating system's credential store when one is available.
